dialogue.text: Some people are disappointed when they first see the most famous painting in the world.
dialogue.zh: 有些人在第一次看到世界上最著名的畫作時會感到失望。
dialogue.ja: 世界で最も有名な絵画を初めて見たとき、がっかりする人もいます。
dialogue.local: Some people are disappointed when they first see the most famous painting in the world.
dialogue.en: Some people are disappointed when they first see the most famous painting in the world.

dialogue.text: At first glance, it doesn't have the wow factor that other paintings in the lube have.
dialogue.zh: 乍看之下，它沒有其他盧浮宮畫作那種令人驚嘆的效果。
dialogue.ja: 一見すると、ルーヴル美術館の他の絵画のような驚きの要素はありません。
dialogue.local: At first glance, it doesn't have the wow factor that other paintings in the lube have.
dialogue.en: At first glance, it doesn't have the wow factor that other paintings in the lube have.

dialogue.text: It lacks drama, but if we can ignore the hundreds of people that surround her, if we can turn down the volume and just push the off button for a second, what we actually see is a quiet contemplative portrait, a portrait that is the greatest psychological portrait ever painted.
dialogue.zh: 它缺乏戲劇性，但如果我們能忽略圍繞她的數百人，暫時關掉喧囂，我們看到的其實是一幅安靜沉思的肖像，是有史以來最偉大的心理肖像畫。
dialogue.ja: ドラマ性は欠けていますが、彼女を取り囲む何百人もの人々を無視し、音量を下げて一瞬だけオフにすると、実際に見えるのは静かで思索的な肖像画であり、これまでに描かれた中で最も優れた心理的肖像画です。
dialogue.local: It lacks drama, but if we can ignore the hundreds of people that surround her, if we can turn down the volume and just push the off button for a second, what we actually see is a quiet contemplative portrait, a portrait that is the greatest psychological portrait ever painted.
dialogue.en: It lacks drama, but if we can ignore the hundreds of people that surround her, if we can turn down the volume and just push the off button for a second, what we actually see is a quiet contemplative portrait, a portrait that is the greatest psychological portrait ever painted.

dialogue.text: A portrait so ahead of its time that centuries later we are still trying to figure it out.
dialogue.zh: 這幅肖像畫超越了它的時代，幾個世紀後我們仍在試圖理解它。
dialogue.ja: 時代を先取りした肖像画で、何世紀も経った今も私たちはその謎を解こうとしています。
dialogue.local: A portrait so ahead of its time that centuries later we are still trying to figure it out.
dialogue.en: A portrait so ahead of its time that centuries later we are still trying to figure it out.

dialogue.text: In 1517, the French king, King Francis I, offered Leonardo a job, court painter and engineer and architect to the king.
dialogue.zh: 1517年，法國國王弗朗索瓦一世邀請達文西擔任宮廷畫家、工程師及國王的建築師。
dialogue.ja: 1517年、フランス王フランソワ1世はレオナルドに宮廷画家、技師、そして王の建築家としての職を提供しました。
dialogue.local: In 1517, the French king, King Francis I, offered Leonardo a job, court painter and engineer and architect to the king.
dialogue.en: In 1517, the French king, King Francis I, offered Leonardo a job, court painter and engineer and architect to the king.

dialogue.text: Leonardo, now in his 60s, moved to the shadow of emboss in France, and never went back to Italy.
dialogue.zh: 當時已六十多歲的達文西搬到了法國昂布瓦斯附近，並且再也沒有回到義大利。
dialogue.ja: 60代になったレオナルドはフランスのアンボワーズの近くに移り、二度とイタリアには戻りませんでした。
dialogue.local: Leonardo, now in his 60s, moved to the shadow of emboss in France, and never went back to Italy.
dialogue.en: Leonardo, now in his 60s, moved to the shadow of emboss in France, and never went back to Italy.

dialogue.text: He brought with him dozens of sketchbooks like these, but just one painting, the Mona Lisa.
dialogue.zh: 他帶來了數十本這樣的素描本，但只有一幅畫作，就是蒙娜麗莎。
dialogue.ja: 彼はこのようなスケッチブックを数十冊持ってきましたが、絵画はモナリザ一枚だけでした。
dialogue.local: He brought with him dozens of sketchbooks like these, but just one painting, the Mona Lisa.
dialogue.en: He brought with him dozens of sketchbooks like these, but just one painting, the Mona Lisa.

dialogue.text: Leonardo knew how important it was, he knew it was a masterpiece.
dialogue.zh: 達文西知道這幅畫的重要性，他知道這是一件傑作。
dialogue.ja: レオナルドはその重要性を理解しており、それが傑作であることを知っていました。
dialogue.local: Leonardo knew how important it was, he knew it was a masterpiece.
dialogue.en: Leonardo knew how important it was, he knew it was a masterpiece.

dialogue.text: Mona Lisa is the end product of the greatest inquisitive mind in history, a self-made man with a voracious appetite for knowledge, a man who dedicated himself to the study of anatomy, geology and philosophy.
dialogue.zh: 蒙娜麗莎是歷史上最偉大好奇心頭腦的結晶，一位自學成才、對知識有強烈渴望，並致力於解剖學、地質學和哲學研究的人所創作。
dialogue.ja: モナリザは歴史上最も探究心旺盛な天才の最終成果であり、解剖学、地質学、哲学の研究に身を捧げた独学の人物によるものです。
dialogue.local: Mona Lisa is the end product of the greatest inquisitive mind in history, a self-made man with a voracious appetite for knowledge, a man who dedicated himself to the study of anatomy, geology and philosophy.
dialogue.en: Mona Lisa is the end product of the greatest inquisitive mind in history, a self-made man with a voracious appetite for knowledge, a man who dedicated himself to the study of anatomy, geology and philosophy.

dialogue.text: For Mona Lisa, he used a thin-grained piece of poplar tree and applied an undercoat of lead white.
dialogue.zh: 為了畫蒙娜麗莎，他使用了一塊細紋的白楊木板，並塗上一層鉛白底漆。
dialogue.ja: モナリザのために、彼は細かい木目のポプラの板を使い、鉛白の下地を塗りました。
dialogue.local: For Mona Lisa, he used a thin-grained piece of poplar tree and applied an undercoat of lead white.
dialogue.en: For Mona Lisa, he used a thin-grained piece of poplar tree and applied an undercoat of lead white.

dialogue.text: Leonardo painted with glazes that had a very small amount of pigment mixed with the oil, so how dark you want your glaze to be depends on how much pigment you use.
dialogue.zh: 達文西使用的釉層中混合了極少量的顏料與油，釉層的深淺取決於顏料的用量。
dialogue.ja: レオナルドはごく少量の顔料を油に混ぜたグレーズで描き、グレーズの濃さは顔料の量によって決まります。
dialogue.local: Leonardo painted with glazes that had a very small amount of pigment mixed with the oil, so how dark you want your glaze to be depends on how much pigment you use.
dialogue.en: Leonardo painted with glazes that had a very small amount of pigment mixed with the oil, so how dark you want your glaze to be depends on how much pigment you use.

dialogue.text: He used more like a wash which he applied thin layer by layer.
dialogue.zh: 他更像是用水洗法，一層層薄薄地塗抹。
dialogue.ja: 彼は薄く何層にも重ねるウォッシュのような技法を使いました。
dialogue.local: He used more like a wash which he applied thin layer by layer.
dialogue.en: He used more like a wash which he applied thin layer by layer.

dialogue.text: Here you can see two colors of contrast, light and dark.
dialogue.zh: 這裡你可以看到兩種對比色，明與暗。
dialogue.ja: ここでは明暗という二つの対照的な色を見ることができます。
dialogue.local: Here you can see two colors of contrast, light and dark.
dialogue.en: Here you can see two colors of contrast, light and dark.

dialogue.text: When you apply glaze over both of them, you can see it starts to unify the contrast, but also brings depth and luminosity.
dialogue.zh: 當你在兩者上塗上釉層時，可以看到對比開始融合，同時帶來深度和光澤。
dialogue.ja: 両方にグレーズを重ねると、対比が統一されるだけでなく、深みと輝きも生まれます。
dialogue.local: When you apply glaze over both of them, you can see it starts to unify the contrast, but also brings depth and luminosity.
dialogue.en: When you apply glaze over both of them, you can see it starts to unify the contrast, but also brings depth and luminosity.

dialogue.text: The lead white undercoat reflects the light back through his glazes, giving the picture more depth and in essence, lighting Mona Lisa from within.
dialogue.zh: 鉛白底漆將光線反射回釉層，賦予畫面更多深度，實質上從內部照亮了蒙娜麗莎。
dialogue.ja: 鉛白の下地が光をグレーズ越しに反射し、絵に深みを与え、モナリザを内側から照らしています。
dialogue.local: The lead white undercoat reflects the light back through his glazes, giving the picture more depth and in essence, lighting Mona Lisa from within.
dialogue.en: The lead white undercoat reflects the light back through his glazes, giving the picture more depth and in essence, lighting Mona Lisa from within.

dialogue.text: As we move around the painting, that light shifts around.
dialogue.zh: 當我們移動觀看畫作時，光線也會隨之變化。
dialogue.ja: 絵の周りを動くと、その光も移動します。
dialogue.local: As we move around the painting, that light shifts around.
dialogue.en: As we move around the painting, that light shifts around.

dialogue.text: He used tiny, almost invisible brushstrokes applied super slowly over months or a Mona Lisa's case years.
dialogue.zh: 他使用極細微、幾乎看不見的筆觸，花費數月甚至數年慢慢完成蒙娜麗莎。
dialogue.ja: 彼は非常に細かくほとんど見えない筆遣いを用い、モナリザの場合は数年かけてゆっくりと描きました。
dialogue.local: He used tiny, almost invisible brushstrokes applied super slowly over months or a Mona Lisa's case years.
dialogue.en: He used tiny, almost invisible brushstrokes applied super slowly over months or a Mona Lisa's case years.

dialogue.text: By contrast, on her skin, the brushstrokes were applied in a irregular way, and that makes the grain of the skin look more lifelike.
dialogue.zh: 相較之下，她皮膚上的筆觸不規則，使皮膚紋理看起來更生動。
dialogue.ja: 対照的に、彼女の肌には不規則な筆遣いがされており、肌の質感がより生き生きと見えます。
dialogue.local: By contrast, on her skin, the brushstrokes were applied in a irregular way, and that makes the grain of the skin look more lifelike.
dialogue.en: By contrast, on her skin, the brushstrokes were applied in a irregular way, and that makes the grain of the skin look more lifelike.

dialogue.text: All of these techniques pioneered by Leonardo bring the painting to life.
dialogue.zh: 所有這些由達文西開創的技術使畫作栩栩如生。
dialogue.ja: これらすべてのレオナルドの技法が絵画に命を吹き込みます。
dialogue.local: All of these techniques pioneered by Leonardo bring the painting to life.
dialogue.en: All of these techniques pioneered by Leonardo bring the painting to life.

dialogue.text: Actually, let's start with what she's not wearing.
dialogue.zh: 其實，我們先來看看她沒有穿什麼。
dialogue.ja: 実は、彼女が身に着けていないものから始めましょう。
dialogue.local: Actually, let's start with what she's not wearing.
dialogue.en: Actually, let's start with what she's not wearing.

dialogue.text: Remember the last time you employed a professional photographer? The answer is usually a wedding or a prom.
dialogue.zh: 還記得你上次請專業攝影師拍照是什麼時候嗎？通常是婚禮或舞會。
dialogue.ja: 最後にプロの写真家を雇ったのはいつですか？多くの場合、結婚式かプロムです。
dialogue.local: Remember the last time you employed a professional photographer? The answer is usually a wedding or a prom.
dialogue.en: Remember the last time you employed a professional photographer? The answer is usually a wedding or a prom.

dialogue.text: What were you wearing in your prom photo? Your best clothes? Your best jewellery? Of course.
dialogue.zh: 你在舞會照片中穿了什麼？最好的衣服？最好的珠寶？當然。
dialogue.ja: プロムの写真では何を着ていましたか？最高の服？最高の宝石？もちろんです。
dialogue.local: What were you wearing in your prom photo? Your best clothes? Your best jewellery? Of course.
dialogue.en: What were you wearing in your prom photo? Your best clothes? Your best jewellery? Of course.

dialogue.text: Being painted by one of the most celebrated and in-demand painters of the day is your chance to really show off.
dialogue.zh: 被當時最著名且搶手的畫家畫肖像，是你真正展示自己的機會。
dialogue.ja: 当時最も有名で需要の高い画家に描かれることは、自分を見せる絶好の機会です。
dialogue.local: Being painted by one of the most celebrated and in-demand painters of the day is your chance to really show off.
dialogue.en: Being painted by one of the most celebrated and in-demand painters of the day is your chance to really show off.

dialogue.text: And yet Mona Lisa is stripped of all the usual high status symbols.
dialogue.zh: 然而蒙娜麗莎卻沒有任何通常象徵高地位的標誌。
dialogue.ja: しかし、モナリザは通常の高い地位を示す象徴をすべて取り除かれています。
dialogue.local: And yet Mona Lisa is stripped of all the usual high status symbols.
dialogue.en: And yet Mona Lisa is stripped of all the usual high status symbols.

dialogue.text: Her clothes are nothing special, they tell us nothing.
dialogue.zh: 她的衣服毫無特別之處，沒有透露任何訊息。
dialogue.ja: 彼女の服は特別なものではなく、何も語っていません。
dialogue.local: Her clothes are nothing special, they tell us nothing.
dialogue.en: Her clothes are nothing special, they tell us nothing.

dialogue.text: Instead of the usual flamboyant expensive outfits we usually see in commissioned portraits of the aristocracy, hers are pretty simple for a wealthy woman.
dialogue.zh: 與貴族委託肖像中常見的華麗昂貴服裝不同，她的衣著對一位富有女性來說相當簡單。
dialogue.ja: 貴族の肖像画でよく見る派手で高価な衣装の代わりに、彼女の服装は裕福な女性としてはかなりシンプルです。
dialogue.local: Instead of the usual flamboyant expensive outfits we usually see in commissioned portraits of the aristocracy, hers are pretty simple for a wealthy woman.
dialogue.en: Instead of the usual flamboyant expensive outfits we usually see in commissioned portraits of the aristocracy, hers are pretty simple for a wealthy woman.

dialogue.text: Along with the complete lack of jewellery and the simple hair, they served one purpose and one purpose only.
dialogue.zh: 加上完全沒有珠寶和簡單的髮型，這些都是為了一個目的。
dialogue.ja: 宝石が全くなく、髪型もシンプルで、それらはただ一つの目的のためにあります。
dialogue.local: Along with the complete lack of jewellery and the simple hair, they served one purpose and one purpose only.
dialogue.en: Along with the complete lack of jewellery and the simple hair, they served one purpose and one purpose only.

dialogue.text: Leonardo made sure we would not be distracted from the face of Mona Lisa.
dialogue.zh: 達文西確保我們不會被蒙娜麗莎的臉以外的東西分心。
dialogue.ja: レオナルドは私たちがモナリザの顔から気をそらされないようにしました。
dialogue.local: Leonardo made sure we would not be distracted from the face of Mona Lisa.
dialogue.en: Leonardo made sure we would not be distracted from the face of Mona Lisa.

dialogue.text: Leonardo uses the classic pyramid shape composition that was introduced during the Renaissance.
dialogue.zh: 達文西使用了文藝復興時期引入的經典金字塔形構圖。
dialogue.ja: レオナルドはルネサンス期に導入された古典的なピラミッド型の構図を使いました。
dialogue.local: Leonardo uses the classic pyramid shape composition that was introduced during the Renaissance.
dialogue.en: Leonardo uses the classic pyramid shape composition that was introduced during the Renaissance.

dialogue.text: It is an important change from the paintings of the 15th century.
dialogue.zh: 這是與15世紀畫作的重要變革。
dialogue.ja: これは15世紀の絵画からの重要な変化です。
dialogue.local: It is an important change from the paintings of the 15th century.
dialogue.en: It is an important change from the paintings of the 15th century.

dialogue.text: The structure provides stability but more importantly it provides a clear centre of focus and directs your gaze.
dialogue.zh: 這種結構提供了穩定性，更重要的是提供了明確的焦點並引導你的視線。
dialogue.ja: この構図は安定感を与えるだけでなく、明確な焦点を作り、視線を誘導します。
dialogue.local: The structure provides stability but more importantly it provides a clear centre of focus and directs your gaze.
dialogue.en: The structure provides stability but more importantly it provides a clear centre of focus and directs your gaze.

dialogue.text: In Mona Lisa's case, it is pulling us into her face.
dialogue.zh: 對蒙娜麗莎而言，它將我們的視線拉向她的臉。
dialogue.ja: モナリザの場合、それは私たちを彼女の顔へ引き込みます。
dialogue.local: In Mona Lisa's case, it is pulling us into her face.
dialogue.en: In Mona Lisa's case, it is pulling us into her face.

dialogue.text: The Mona Lisa is the earliest Italian portrait to focus on the sitter in a three-quarter length pose rather than full length.
dialogue.zh: 蒙娜麗莎是最早聚焦於三分之三身像而非全身像的義大利肖像畫。
dialogue.ja: モナリザは、全身ではなく三四分の三のポーズに焦点を当てた最も古いイタリアの肖像画です。
dialogue.local: The Mona Lisa is the earliest Italian portrait to focus on the sitter in a three-quarter length pose rather than full length.
dialogue.en: The Mona Lisa is the earliest Italian portrait to focus on the sitter in a three-quarter length pose rather than full length.

dialogue.text: But why? Because he completely fills the frame with his subject, making the painting more intimate and cutting down on distractions.
dialogue.zh: 為什麼？因為他將畫面完全填滿主角，使畫作更親密且減少干擾。
dialogue.ja: なぜなら、彼は画面を被写体で完全に満たし、絵をより親密にし、気を散らすものを減らしたからです。
dialogue.local: But why? Because he completely fills the frame with his subject, making the painting more intimate and cutting down on distractions.
dialogue.en: But why? Because he completely fills the frame with his subject, making the painting more intimate and cutting down on distractions.

dialogue.text: This three-quarter length pose becomes the norm for 400 years after Leonardo pioneers it.
dialogue.zh: 這種三分之三身像的姿勢成為達文西開創後400年的標準。
dialogue.ja: この三四分の三のポーズは、レオナルドが先駆けてから400年間の標準となりました。
dialogue.local: This three-quarter length pose becomes the norm for 400 years after Leonardo pioneers it.
dialogue.en: This three-quarter length pose becomes the norm for 400 years after Leonardo pioneers it.

dialogue.text: Today we look at Mona Lisa's pose and it seems fairly normal, but for its day it was groundbreaking.
dialogue.zh: 今天看蒙娜麗莎的姿勢很普通，但在當時卻是突破性的。
dialogue.ja: 今日見るとモナリザのポーズは普通に見えますが、当時は画期的でした。
dialogue.local: Today we look at Mona Lisa's pose and it seems fairly normal, but for its day it was groundbreaking.
dialogue.en: Today we look at Mona Lisa's pose and it seems fairly normal, but for its day it was groundbreaking.

dialogue.text: Previously subjects were stiff an upright aristocratic, but Mona Lisa is relaxed.
dialogue.zh: 以前的肖像主題通常僵硬端正且貴族氣息濃厚，但蒙娜麗莎顯得輕鬆自然。
dialogue.ja: 以前は被写体は堅苦しく直立した貴族的なものでしたが、モナリザはリラックスしています。
dialogue.local: Previously subjects were stiff an upright aristocratic, but Mona Lisa is relaxed.
dialogue.en: Previously subjects were stiff an upright aristocratic, but Mona Lisa is relaxed.

dialogue.text: Her hands are resting gently on the arm of her chair as she turns towards us, almost as if it's a snapshot.
dialogue.zh: 她的雙手輕輕放在椅子扶手上，轉向我們，彷彿一張快照。
dialogue.ja: 彼女の手は椅子の肘掛けに優しく置かれ、こちらに向いていて、まるでスナップ写真のようです。
dialogue.local: Her hands are resting gently on the arm of her chair as she turns towards us, almost as if it's a snapshot.
dialogue.en: Her hands are resting gently on the arm of her chair as she turns towards us, almost as if it's a snapshot.

dialogue.text: Mona Lisa is also rather content and self-assured, which was more how aristocratic men were portrayed, not women.
dialogue.zh: 蒙娜麗莎看起來相當滿足且自信，這種形象過去多用於描繪貴族男性，而非女性。
dialogue.ja: モナリザは満足そうで自信に満ちており、これは貴族の男性が描かれる時の特徴であり、女性には珍しいものでした。
dialogue.local: Mona Lisa is also rather content and self-assured, which was more how aristocratic men were portrayed, not women.
dialogue.en: Mona Lisa is also rather content and self-assured, which was more how aristocratic men were portrayed, not women.

dialogue.text: We are looking directly into her eyes and she is looking directly at us.
dialogue.zh: 我們直視她的眼睛，她也直視著我們。
dialogue.ja: 私たちは彼女の目を直接見つめ、彼女も私たちを直接見ています。
dialogue.local: We are looking directly into her eyes and she is looking directly at us.
dialogue.en: We are looking directly into her eyes and she is looking directly at us.

dialogue.text: Women in paintings just didn't do that.
dialogue.zh: 畫中的女性以前不會這樣做。
dialogue.ja: 絵画の中の女性はそうはしませんでした。
dialogue.local: Women in paintings just didn't do that.
dialogue.en: Women in paintings just didn't do that.

dialogue.text: They didn't look boldly and directly at the viewer.
dialogue.zh: 她們不會大膽且直接地看著觀者。
dialogue.ja: 彼女たちは大胆に直接観る人を見つめることはありませんでした。
dialogue.local: They didn't look boldly and directly at the viewer.
dialogue.en: They didn't look boldly and directly at the viewer.

dialogue.text: The entire painting deviated from the traditional way women were painted in Italy.
dialogue.zh: 整幅畫偏離了義大利傳統女性肖像的繪畫方式。
dialogue.ja: この絵はイタリアで女性が描かれてきた伝統的な方法から逸脱しています。
dialogue.local: The entire painting deviated from the traditional way women were painted in Italy.
dialogue.en: The entire painting deviated from the traditional way women were painted in Italy.

dialogue.text: Portraits were usually drawn with an open sky as the background, a monotone background or a simple room.
dialogue.zh: 肖像畫通常以開闊的天空、單色背景或簡單的房間作為背景。
dialogue.ja: 肖像画は通常、開けた空、単色の背景、またはシンプルな部屋を背景に描かれていました。
dialogue.local: Portraits were usually drawn with an open sky as the background, a monotone background or a simple room.
dialogue.en: Portraits were usually drawn with an open sky as the background, a monotone background or a simple room.

dialogue.text: Mona Lisa is in front of a complicated landscape that only existed in Leonardo's imagination.
dialogue.zh: 蒙娜麗莎前方是只有達文西想像中存在的複雜景觀。
dialogue.ja: モナリザの背後には、レオナルドの想像の中にしか存在しない複雑な風景があります。
dialogue.local: Mona Lisa is in front of a complicated landscape that only existed in Leonardo's imagination.
dialogue.en: Mona Lisa is in front of a complicated landscape that only existed in Leonardo's imagination.

dialogue.text: Paintings of this period had both the subject and the background in sharp focus, whereas the background of the Mona Lisa seems to fade or become more blurred and out of focus the further from the subjects it extends.
dialogue.zh: 這個時期的畫作主題和背景都清晰聚焦，而蒙娜麗莎的背景則隨距離主體越遠而逐漸模糊失焦。
dialogue.ja: この時代の絵画は被写体と背景の両方が鮮明でしたが、モナリザの背景は被写体から離れるほどぼやけて焦点が合っていません。
dialogue.local: Paintings of this period had both the subject and the background in sharp focus, whereas the background of the Mona Lisa seems to fade or become more blurred and out of focus the further from the subjects it extends.
dialogue.en: Paintings of this period had both the subject and the background in sharp focus, whereas the background of the Mona Lisa seems to fade or become more blurred and out of focus the further from the subjects it extends.

dialogue.text: This is aerial perspective and Leonardo invented it.
dialogue.zh: 這是空氣透視法，達文西發明的。
dialogue.ja: これは空気遠近法で、レオナルドが発明しました。
dialogue.local: This is aerial perspective and Leonardo invented it.
dialogue.en: This is aerial perspective and Leonardo invented it.

dialogue.text: Behind Mona Lisa the vast landscape recedes to distant icy mountains.
dialogue.zh: 蒙娜麗莎背後的廣闊景觀延伸至遙遠的冰冷山脈。
dialogue.ja: モナリザの後ろには広大な風景が遠くの氷山へと続いています。
dialogue.local: Behind Mona Lisa the vast landscape recedes to distant icy mountains.
dialogue.en: Behind Mona Lisa the vast landscape recedes to distant icy mountains.

dialogue.text: A path and a bridge are our only indication of human presence.
dialogue.zh: 一條小徑和一座橋是唯一顯示有人類存在的跡象。
dialogue.ja: 小道と橋だけが人間の存在を示しています。
dialogue.local: A path and a bridge are our only indication of human presence.
dialogue.en: A path and a bridge are our only indication of human presence.

dialogue.text: The curves of her hair and clothing reflect the rolling valleys and rivers behind her, connecting humanity and nature, a favourite theme of Leonardo's.
dialogue.zh: 她的頭髮和衣服的曲線反映了背後起伏的山谷和河流，連結了人類與自然，這是達文西喜愛的主題。
dialogue.ja: 彼女の髪と服の曲線は背後の谷や川の起伏を反映し、人間と自然をつなげています。これはレオナルドのお気に入りのテーマです。
dialogue.local: The curves of her hair and clothing reflect the rolling valleys and rivers behind her, connecting humanity and nature, a favourite theme of Leonardo's.
dialogue.en: The curves of her hair and clothing reflect the rolling valleys and rivers behind her, connecting humanity and nature, a favourite theme of Leonardo's.

dialogue.text: The earth seems to twist like her torso.
dialogue.zh: 大地似乎像她的軀幹一樣扭曲。
dialogue.ja: 大地は彼女の胴体のようにねじれているように見えます。
dialogue.local: The earth seems to twist like her torso.
dialogue.en: The earth seems to twist like her torso.

dialogue.text: Look at the river on the right. It flows into the scarf over her left shoulder.
dialogue.zh: 看看右邊的河流，它流入她左肩上的圍巾。
dialogue.ja: 右側の川を見てください。それは彼女の左肩のスカーフに流れ込んでいます。
dialogue.local: Look at the river on the right. It flows into the scarf over her left shoulder.
dialogue.en: Look at the river on the right. It flows into the scarf over her left shoulder.

dialogue.text: We see that she is connected with the earth.
dialogue.zh: 我們看到她與大地相連。
dialogue.ja: 彼女が大地とつながっているのがわかります。
dialogue.local: We see that she is connected with the earth.
dialogue.en: We see that she is connected with the earth.

dialogue.text: There is another visual trick that gives an illusion of movement.
dialogue.zh: 還有另一個視覺技巧，營造出動態幻覺。
dialogue.ja: 動きを感じさせる別の視覚的なトリックがあります。
dialogue.local: There is another visual trick that gives an illusion of movement.
dialogue.en: There is another visual trick that gives an illusion of movement.

dialogue.text: The horizon of the landscape does not quite line up behind the figure.
dialogue.zh: 景觀的地平線與人物背後的位置不完全對齊。
dialogue.ja: 風景の地平線は人物の背後で完全に一致していません。
dialogue.local: The horizon of the landscape does not quite line up behind the figure.
dialogue.en: The horizon of the landscape does not quite line up behind the figure.

dialogue.text: It is very slightly skewed whilst her shoulders are painted level.
dialogue.zh: 地平線稍微傾斜，而她的肩膀卻是水平畫的。
dialogue.ja: 地平線はわずかに傾いていますが、彼女の肩は水平に描かれています。
dialogue.local: It is very slightly skewed whilst her shoulders are painted level.
dialogue.en: It is very slightly skewed whilst her shoulders are painted level.

dialogue.text: Leonardo knew that our brains would struggle with this conflicting visual information.
dialogue.zh: 達文西知道我們的大腦會難以處理這種矛盾的視覺訊息。
dialogue.ja: レオナルドは私たちの脳がこの矛盾する視覚情報に苦労することを知っていました。
dialogue.local: Leonardo knew that our brains would struggle with this conflicting visual information.
dialogue.en: Leonardo knew that our brains would struggle with this conflicting visual information.

dialogue.text: We know that the horizon should line up so we read it as level.
dialogue.zh: 我們知道地平線應該對齊，因此會視為水平。
dialogue.ja: 地平線は揃っているはずだと認識し、それを水平と読み取ります。
dialogue.local: We know that the horizon should line up so we read it as level.
dialogue.en: We know that the horizon should line up so we read it as level.

dialogue.text: This then causes us to interpret the shoulders as being on a slant, which they are not.
dialogue.zh: 這使我們誤以為肩膀傾斜，但實際上並沒有。
dialogue.ja: そのため、肩が傾いていると解釈しますが、実際はそうではありません。
dialogue.local: This then causes us to interpret the shoulders as being on a slant, which they are not.
dialogue.en: This then causes us to interpret the shoulders as being on a slant, which they are not.

dialogue.text: As our brain corrects this, it creates an illusion of movement as if the figure shuffles a little bit in its frame.
dialogue.zh: 當我們的大腦修正這點時，會產生動態幻覺，彷彿人物在畫框中微微移動。
dialogue.ja: 脳がこれを修正すると、人物が額縁の中で少し動いているような錯覚が生まれます。
dialogue.local: As our brain corrects this, it creates an illusion of movement as if the figure shuffles a little bit in its frame.
dialogue.en: As our brain corrects this, it creates an illusion of movement as if the figure shuffles a little bit in its frame.

dialogue.text: The effect only works with paintings, not sculptures or real life, since the elements of perspective and light and shadow are fixed in a painting and don't change, they look the same no matter from what angle you look at it.
dialogue.zh: 這種效果只對畫作有效，雕塑或現實生活中無效，因為畫中的透視、光影是固定不變的，無論從哪個角度看都一樣。
dialogue.ja: この効果は絵画にのみ有効で、彫刻や実物では効果がありません。絵画の透視や光と影の要素は固定されており、どの角度から見ても同じに見えます。
dialogue.local: The effect only works with paintings, not sculptures or real life, since the elements of perspective and light and shadow are fixed in a painting and don't change, they look the same no matter from what angle you look at it.
dialogue.en: The effect only works with paintings, not sculptures or real life, since the elements of perspective and light and shadow are fixed in a painting and don't change, they look the same no matter from what angle you look at it.

dialogue.text: It's a real phenomena but not unique to this painting.
dialogue.zh: 這是真實的現象，但並非此畫獨有。
dialogue.ja: これは実際の現象ですが、この絵画だけに特有のものではありません。
dialogue.local: It's a real phenomena but not unique to this painting.
dialogue.en: It's a real phenomena but not unique to this painting.

dialogue.text: The first technique he invented was somato, meaning smoky.
dialogue.zh: 他發明的第一種技法是煙霧法（somato），意指煙霧狀。
dialogue.ja: 彼が発明した最初の技法はスフマート（煙のような意味）です。
dialogue.local: The first technique he invented was somato, meaning smoky.
dialogue.en: The first technique he invented was somato, meaning smoky.

dialogue.text: Somato is a blending technique for softening the transition between colors to make sure there are no sharp unnatural lines.
dialogue.zh: 煙霧法是一種混色技術，用來柔化色彩過渡，避免出現銳利不自然的線條。
dialogue.ja: スフマートは色の境界を柔らかくぼかし、鋭い不自然な線をなくすための混色技法です。
dialogue.local: Somato is a blending technique for softening the transition between colors to make sure there are no sharp unnatural lines.
dialogue.en: Somato is a blending technique for softening the transition between colors to make sure there are no sharp unnatural lines.

dialogue.text: Through layers and layers of those thin semi-transparent glazes, he blended everything somato style.
dialogue.zh: 他透過一層又一層薄薄半透明的釉層，以煙霧法混合所有色彩。
dialogue.ja: 彼は薄く半透明のグレーズを何層にも重ねて、すべてをスフマートのスタイルでぼかしました。
dialogue.local: Through layers and layers of those thin semi-transparent glazes, he blended everything somato style.
dialogue.en: Through layers and layers of those thin semi-transparent glazes, he blended everything somato style.

dialogue.text: His brush strokes so subtle as to be invisible to the naked eye.
dialogue.zh: 他的筆觸細膩到肉眼幾乎看不見。
dialogue.ja: 彼の筆遣いは非常に繊細で、肉眼ではほとんど見えません。
dialogue.local: His brush strokes so subtle as to be invisible to the naked eye.
dialogue.en: His brush strokes so subtle as to be invisible to the naked eye.

dialogue.text: In essence, the somato technique takes painting one stage further.
dialogue.zh: 本質上，煙霧法使繪畫更上一層樓。
dialogue.ja: 本質的に、スフマート技法は絵画を一段階進化させます。
dialogue.local: In essence, the somato technique takes painting one stage further.
dialogue.en: In essence, the somato technique takes painting one stage further.

dialogue.text: It allows us to look at a painting the way our eyes work tonally.
dialogue.zh: 它讓我們以眼睛感知色調的方式來觀看畫作。
dialogue.ja: それは私たちが目で色調を認識する方法で絵を見ることを可能にします。
dialogue.local: It allows us to look at a painting the way our eyes work tonally.
dialogue.en: It allows us to look at a painting the way our eyes work tonally.

dialogue.text: It allows depth of field, never seen in a painting before Mona Lisa.
dialogue.zh: 它創造了景深效果，蒙娜麗莎之前的畫作從未見過。
dialogue.ja: それは被写界深度を可能にし、モナリザ以前の絵画では見られませんでした。
dialogue.local: It allows depth of field, never seen in a painting before Mona Lisa.
dialogue.en: It allows depth of field, never seen in a painting before Mona Lisa.

dialogue.text: We can see what a master of the somato he was when we look at the shading around Mona Lisa's eyes.
dialogue.zh: 當我們看蒙娜麗莎眼周的陰影時，可以看出他是煙霧法的大師。
dialogue.ja: モナリザの目の周りの陰影を見ると、彼がスフマートの名手であったことがわかります。
dialogue.local: We can see what a master of the somato he was when we look at the shading around Mona Lisa's eyes.
dialogue.en: We can see what a master of the somato he was when we look at the shading around Mona Lisa's eyes.

dialogue.text: The other technique he invented is Kiara Squirtle from the Italian for light dark, where he contrasts prominent shades of light and dark to create the illusion of three dimensional forms.
dialogue.zh: 他發明的另一種技法是義大利語的明暗對比法（Chiaroscuro），透過強烈的明暗對比創造三維立體感。
dialogue.ja: 彼が発明したもう一つの技法はイタリア語で明暗を意味するキアロスクーロで、明暗の強い対比で立体感を生み出します。
dialogue.local: The other technique he invented is Kiara Squirtle from the Italian for light dark, where he contrasts prominent shades of light and dark to create the illusion of three dimensional forms.
dialogue.en: The other technique he invented is Kiara Squirtle from the Italian for light dark, where he contrasts prominent shades of light and dark to create the illusion of three dimensional forms.

dialogue.text: Seeing Mona Lisa for the first time 500 years ago must have been astonishing.
dialogue.zh: 500年前首次見到蒙娜麗莎一定令人驚嘆。
dialogue.ja: 500年前に初めてモナリザを見た人は驚嘆したことでしょう。
dialogue.local: Seeing Mona Lisa for the first time 500 years ago must have been astonishing.
dialogue.en: Seeing Mona Lisa for the first time 500 years ago must have been astonishing.

dialogue.text: Then there is the smile that pulls everything together.
dialogue.zh: 還有那個將一切串連起來的微笑。
dialogue.ja: そして、すべてをまとめる微笑みがあります。
dialogue.local: Then there is the smile that pulls everything together.
dialogue.en: Then there is the smile that pulls everything together.

dialogue.text: Before, during and long after the Renaissance, artists did not paint their subject smiling.
dialogue.zh: 文藝復興前後及其後很長一段時間，藝術家都不會畫主角微笑的樣子。
dialogue.ja: ルネサンスの前後、そしてその後長い間、芸術家は被写体を笑顔で描きませんでした。
dialogue.local: Before, during and long after the Renaissance, artists did not paint their subject smiling.
dialogue.en: Before, during and long after the Renaissance, artists did not paint their subject smiling.

dialogue.text: When you think about it, portraits are generally very serious.
dialogue.zh: 仔細想想，肖像畫通常都很嚴肅。
dialogue.ja: よく考えると、肖像画は一般的に非常に真面目です。
dialogue.local: When you think about it, portraits are generally very serious.
dialogue.en: When you think about it, portraits are generally very serious.

dialogue.text: It's easy enough to smile for a few minutes but not for the weeks if not months it takes to paint a portrait.
dialogue.zh: 微笑幾分鐘很容易，但畫肖像畫需要數週甚至數月，難以持續微笑。
dialogue.ja: 数分間笑うのは簡単ですが、肖像画を描くのに数週間、場合によっては数ヶ月かかるため、ずっと笑い続けるのは難しいです。
dialogue.local: It's easy enough to smile for a few minutes but not for the weeks if not months it takes to paint a portrait.
dialogue.en: It's easy enough to smile for a few minutes but not for the weeks if not months it takes to paint a portrait.

dialogue.text: Leonardo kept her happy though by employing musicians and gestures.
dialogue.zh: 不過達文西透過請音樂家和手勢讓她保持愉快。
dialogue.ja: レオナルドは音楽家やジェスチャーを使って彼女を楽しませ、笑顔を保たせました。
dialogue.local: Leonardo kept her happy though by employing musicians and gestures.
dialogue.en: Leonardo kept her happy though by employing musicians and gestures.

dialogue.text: Look at her for a while. Really look into her eyes.
dialogue.zh: 看著她一會兒，真的注視她的眼睛。
dialogue.ja: しばらく彼女を見てください。本当に彼女の目を見つめてください。
dialogue.local: Look at her for a while. Really look into her eyes.
dialogue.en: Look at her for a while. Really look into her eyes.

dialogue.text: First she is smiling and then she is not.
dialogue.zh: 她的微笑時而出現，時而消失。
dialogue.ja: 最初は笑っていて、次に笑っていません。
dialogue.local: First she is smiling and then she is not.
dialogue.en: First she is smiling and then she is not.

dialogue.text: The smile comes and goes as we scan the face.
dialogue.zh: 當我們掃視她的臉時，微笑忽隱忽現。
dialogue.ja: 顔を見ていると、笑顔が現れたり消えたりします。
dialogue.local: The smile comes and goes as we scan the face.
dialogue.en: The smile comes and goes as we scan the face.

dialogue.text: But when we look away, the smile lingers.
dialogue.zh: 但當我們移開視線，微笑仍留存。
dialogue.ja: しかし、目をそらすと笑顔が残ります。
dialogue.local: But when we look away, the smile lingers.
dialogue.en: But when we look away, the smile lingers.

dialogue.text: When Leonardo was perfecting Lisa's smile, he was spending his nights in the morgue, peeling the flesh off cadavers and exposing the muscles and nerves underneath.
dialogue.zh: 當達文西完善麗莎的微笑時，他夜晚待在太平間，剝離屍體的肌膚，暴露下面的肌肉和神經。
dialogue.ja: レオナルドがリサの笑顔を完成させていた頃、彼は夜を検視室で過ごし、死体の肉を剥がして筋肉や神経を露出させていました。
dialogue.local: When Leonardo was perfecting Lisa's smile, he was spending his nights in the morgue, peeling the flesh off cadavers and exposing the muscles and nerves underneath.
dialogue.en: When Leonardo was perfecting Lisa's smile, he was spending his nights in the morgue, peeling the flesh off cadavers and exposing the muscles and nerves underneath.

dialogue.text: He became fascinated by how a smile works and analysed every possible movement of each part of the face, working out the origins of every nerve that controls every facial muscle.
dialogue.zh: 他對微笑的運作著迷，分析臉部每個部位的每個可能動作，找出控制每條臉部肌肉的神經起源。
dialogue.ja: 彼は笑顔の仕組みに魅了され、顔の各部分のあらゆる動きを分析し、顔の筋肉を制御する神経の起源を解明しました。
dialogue.local: He became fascinated by how a smile works and analysed every possible movement of each part of the face, working out the origins of every nerve that controls every facial muscle.
dialogue.en: He became fascinated by how a smile works and analysed every possible movement of each part of the face, working out the origins of every nerve that controls every facial muscle.

dialogue.text: We can see this research in his anatomical drawings.
dialogue.zh: 我們可以在他的解剖學素描中看到這些研究。
dialogue.ja: 彼の解剖学的な図面にこの研究を見ることができます。
dialogue.local: We can see this research in his anatomical drawings.
dialogue.en: We can see this research in his anatomical drawings.

dialogue.text: Here we see puckered lips, pouting lips, the muscles that move the mouth.
dialogue.zh: 這裡我們看到皺起的嘴唇、噘嘴，以及控制嘴巴動作的肌肉。
dialogue.ja: ここにはすぼめた唇、突き出した唇、口を動かす筋肉が描かれています。
dialogue.local: Here we see puckered lips, pouting lips, the muscles that move the mouth.
dialogue.en: Here we see puckered lips, pouting lips, the muscles that move the mouth.

dialogue.text: Then almost forgotten at the top of this page is a simple drawing of a gentle smile, sketch lightly in black chalk.
dialogue.zh: 然後在這頁頂端幾乎被忽略的是一幅輕描淡寫的黑色粉筆溫柔微笑素描。
dialogue.ja: そしてこのページの上部には、ほとんど忘れられている軽く描かれた優しい笑顔のスケッチがあります。
dialogue.local: Then almost forgotten at the top of this page is a simple drawing of a gentle smile, sketch lightly in black chalk.
dialogue.en: Then almost forgotten at the top of this page is a simple drawing of a gentle smile, sketch lightly in black chalk.

dialogue.text: Even though the fine lines at the end of the mouth turned down slightly, the feeling is that the lips are smiling.
dialogue.zh: 儘管嘴角的細線微微向下，但感覺嘴唇仍在微笑。
dialogue.ja: 口の端の細い線はわずかに下がっていますが、唇は笑っているように感じられます。
dialogue.local: Even though the fine lines at the end of the mouth turned down slightly, the feeling is that the lips are smiling.
dialogue.en: Even though the fine lines at the end of the mouth turned down slightly, the feeling is that the lips are smiling.

dialogue.text: This simple anatomical drawing is the beginning of Mona Lisa's smile.
dialogue.zh: 這幅簡單的解剖素描是蒙娜麗莎微笑的起點。
dialogue.ja: このシンプルな解剖学的な図はモナリザの笑顔の始まりです。
dialogue.local: This simple anatomical drawing is the beginning of Mona Lisa's smile.
dialogue.en: This simple anatomical drawing is the beginning of Mona Lisa's smile.

dialogue.text: Astonishingly, Leonardo already knew from his optics studies that light rays do not come to a single point in the eye but instead hit the whole area of the retina.
dialogue.zh: 令人驚訝的是，達文西從他的光學研究中已知光線不會聚焦於眼睛的單一點，而是照射整個視網膜區域。
dialogue.ja: 驚くべきことに、レオナルドは光学の研究から、光線は目の一点に集まるのではなく、網膜全体に当たることを知っていました。
dialogue.local: Astonishingly, Leonardo already knew from his optics studies that light rays do not come to a single point in the eye but instead hit the whole area of the retina.
dialogue.en: Astonishingly, Leonardo already knew from his optics studies that light rays do not come to a single point in the eye but instead hit the whole area of the retina.

dialogue.text: And this is the key to her enigmatic smile.
dialogue.zh: 這就是她神秘微笑的關鍵。
dialogue.ja: これが彼女の謎めいた笑顔の鍵です。
dialogue.local: And this is the key to her enigmatic smile.
dialogue.en: And this is the key to her enigmatic smile.

dialogue.text: In the year 2000, Dr Margaret Livingston, a Harvard neuroscientist, discovered that Mona Lisa's smile comes and goes because of how the human visual system is designed, not because the expression is ambiguous.
dialogue.zh: 2000年，哈佛神經科學家瑪格麗特·利文斯頓博士發現蒙娜麗莎的微笑忽隱忽現，是因為人類視覺系統的設計，而非表情模糊。
dialogue.ja: 2000年、ハーバードの神経科学者マーガレット・リビングストン博士は、モナリザの笑顔が消えたり現れたりするのは表情が曖昧だからではなく、人間の視覚システムの設計によることを発見しました。
dialogue.local: In the year 2000, Dr Margaret Livingston, a Harvard neuroscientist, discovered that Mona Lisa's smile comes and goes because of how the human visual system is designed, not because the expression is ambiguous.
dialogue.en: In the year 2000, Dr Margaret Livingston, a Harvard neuroscientist, discovered that Mona Lisa's smile comes and goes because of how the human visual system is designed, not because the expression is ambiguous.

dialogue.text: She explained that the human eye has two distinct regions for seeing the world.
dialogue.zh: 她解釋人眼有兩個不同區域用來看世界。
dialogue.ja: 彼女は人間の目には世界を見るための二つの異なる領域があると説明しました。
dialogue.local: She explained that the human eye has two distinct regions for seeing the world.
dialogue.en: She explained that the human eye has two distinct regions for seeing the world.

dialogue.text: A central area called the phobia is where people see colours, read fine print and pick out details.
dialogue.zh: 中央區域稱為黃斑，人們在這裡看見顏色、閱讀細字和辨識細節。
dialogue.ja: 中心部の黄斑と呼ばれる領域では、人は色を見たり、細かい文字を読んだり、詳細を識別したりします。
dialogue.local: A central area called the phobia is where people see colours, read fine print and pick out details.
dialogue.en: A central area called the phobia is where people see colours, read fine print and pick out details.

dialogue.text: And the peripheral area surrounding the phobia is where people see black and white, motion and shadows.
dialogue.zh: 而圍繞黃斑的周邊區域，人們看到的是黑白、運動和陰影。
dialogue.ja: 黄斑を囲む周辺部では、人は白黒や動き、影を見ます。
dialogue.local: And the peripheral area surrounding the phobia is where people see black and white, motion and shadows.
dialogue.en: And the peripheral area surrounding the phobia is where people see black and white, motion and shadows.

dialogue.text: When we look at a face, we spend most of the time focused on the other person's eyes.
dialogue.zh: 當我們看一張臉時，大部分時間都專注於對方的眼睛。
dialogue.ja: 顔を見るとき、私たちはほとんどの時間を相手の目に集中しています。
dialogue.local: When we look at a face, we spend most of the time focused on the other person's eyes.
dialogue.en: When we look at a face, we spend most of the time focused on the other person's eyes.

dialogue.text: So when a person's centre of gaze is on Mona Lisa's eyes, the less accurate peripheral vision is on her mouth.
dialogue.zh: 所以當視線集中在蒙娜麗莎的眼睛時，較不精確的周邊視野會落在她的嘴巴上。
dialogue.ja: だから視線の中心がモナリザの目にあるとき、あまり正確でない周辺視野は彼女の口に向かいます。
dialogue.local: So when a person's centre of gaze is on Mona Lisa's eyes, the less accurate peripheral vision is on her mouth.
dialogue.en: So when a person's centre of gaze is on Mona Lisa's eyes, the less accurate peripheral vision is on her mouth.

dialogue.text: And because peripheral vision is not interested in specific details, it also picks up shadows from Mona Lisa's cheekbones.
dialogue.zh: 而周邊視野不關注細節，也會捕捉到蒙娜麗莎顴骨的陰影。
dialogue.ja: 周辺視野は細かい詳細に興味がないため、モナリザの頬骨の影も捉えます。
dialogue.local: And because peripheral vision is not interested in specific details, it also picks up shadows from Mona Lisa's cheekbones.
dialogue.en: And because peripheral vision is not interested in specific details, it also picks up shadows from Mona Lisa's cheekbones.

dialogue.text: This is where both his swoomato and Kiaroscoro techniques come into their own.
dialogue.zh: 這正是他的煙霧法和明暗對比法發揮作用的地方。
dialogue.ja: ここで彼のスフマートとキアロスクーロの技法が活きてきます。
dialogue.local: This is where both his swoomato and Kiaroscoro techniques come into their own.
dialogue.en: This is where both his swoomato and Kiaroscoro techniques come into their own.

dialogue.text: As we look into her eyes, the shadows and tones suggest the curvature of a smile.
dialogue.zh: 當我們注視她的眼睛時，陰影和色調暗示著微笑的弧度。
dialogue.ja: 彼女の目を見つめると、影や色調が笑顔の曲線を示唆します。
dialogue.local: As we look into her eyes, the shadows and tones suggest the curvature of a smile.
dialogue.en: As we look into her eyes, the shadows and tones suggest the curvature of a smile.

dialogue.text: But when your eyes go directly to Mona Lisa's mouth, your central vision doesn't see the shadows and she isn't smiling.
dialogue.zh: 但當你的視線直接看向蒙娜麗莎的嘴巴時，中央視野看不到陰影，她並沒有微笑。
dialogue.ja: しかし、目を直接モナリザの口に向けると、中心視野は影を見ず、彼女は笑っていません。
dialogue.local: But when your eyes go directly to Mona Lisa's mouth, your central vision doesn't see the shadows and she isn't smiling.
dialogue.en: But when your eyes go directly to Mona Lisa's mouth, your central vision doesn't see the shadows and she isn't smiling.

dialogue.text: Smurking at best.
dialogue.zh: 頂多是嘟嘴。
dialogue.ja: せいぜいしかめっ面です。
dialogue.local: Smurking at best.
dialogue.en: Smurking at best.

dialogue.text: We can prove this theory quite simply by staring directly into her eyes and think about how much she is smiling.
dialogue.zh: 我們可以簡單地透過直視她的眼睛，思考她微笑的程度來證明這個理論。
dialogue.ja: 彼女の目をじっと見つめて、どれだけ笑っているか考えることで、この理論を簡単に証明できます。
dialogue.local: We can prove this theory quite simply by staring directly into her eyes and think about how much she is smiling.
dialogue.en: We can prove this theory quite simply by staring directly into her eyes and think about how much she is smiling.

dialogue.text: Then scan back and forth between her eyes and her lips and her expression changes.
dialogue.zh: 然後在她的眼睛和嘴唇之間來回掃視，她的表情會改變。
dialogue.ja: 次に彼女の目と唇の間を行き来すると、表情が変わります。
dialogue.local: Then scan back and forth between her eyes and her lips and her expression changes.
dialogue.en: Then scan back and forth between her eyes and her lips and her expression changes.

dialogue.text: That is not your imagination. It is all to do with how we see, not how we think.
dialogue.zh: 這不是你的想像，完全是因為我們的視覺方式，而非思考方式。
dialogue.ja: それはあなたの想像ではなく、私たちの見え方に関係しているのであって、考え方ではありません。
dialogue.local: That is not your imagination. It is all to do with how we see, not how we think.
dialogue.en: That is not your imagination. It is all to do with how we see, not how we think.

dialogue.text: The genius of Leonardo is that he understood this 500 years ago.
dialogue.zh: 達文西的天才在於他500年前就理解了這點。
dialogue.ja: レオナルドの天才は、500年前にこれを理解していたことです。
dialogue.local: The genius of Leonardo is that he understood this 500 years ago.
dialogue.en: The genius of Leonardo is that he understood this 500 years ago.

dialogue.text: The Mona Lisa became the most famous painting in the world, not just because of hype or chance, but because for 500 years, viewers have been able to feel an emotional engagement with her.
dialogue.zh: 蒙娜麗莎成為世界上最著名的畫作，不僅因為炒作或偶然，而是因為500年來觀者能與她產生情感共鳴。
dialogue.ja: モナリザが世界で最も有名な絵画になったのは、宣伝や偶然だけでなく、500年間にわたり鑑賞者が彼女と感情的なつながりを感じられたからです。
dialogue.local: The Mona Lisa became the most famous painting in the world, not just because of hype or chance, but because for 500 years, viewers have been able to feel an emotional engagement with her.
dialogue.en: The Mona Lisa became the most famous painting in the world, not just because of hype or chance, but because for 500 years, viewers have been able to feel an emotional engagement with her.

dialogue.text: Before the Mona Lisa, portraits lacked mystery, artists only represented outward appearances.
dialogue.zh: 在蒙娜麗莎之前，肖像畫缺乏神秘感，藝術家只描繪外表。
dialogue.ja: モナリザ以前、肖像画には神秘性がなく、芸術家は外見だけを表現していました。
dialogue.local: Before the Mona Lisa, portraits lacked mystery, artists only represented outward appearances.
dialogue.en: Before the Mona Lisa, portraits lacked mystery, artists only represented outward appearances.

dialogue.text: Mona Lisa, however, is alive, a living, breathing woman with a soul.
dialogue.zh: 然而蒙娜麗莎是有生命、有靈魂的活生生的女人。
dialogue.ja: しかしモナリザは生きていて、魂を持つ生き生きとした女性です。
dialogue.local: Mona Lisa, however, is alive, a living, breathing woman with a soul.
dialogue.en: Mona Lisa, however, is alive, a living, breathing woman with a soul.

dialogue.text: When you stand in front of the Mona Lisa, you are looking at more than just a portrait of an individual.
dialogue.zh: 當你站在蒙娜麗莎面前，你看到的不僅僅是一個人的肖像。
dialogue.ja: モナリザの前に立つとき、あなたは単なる個人の肖像以上のものを見ています。
dialogue.local: When you stand in front of the Mona Lisa, you are looking at more than just a portrait of an individual.
dialogue.en: When you stand in front of the Mona Lisa, you are looking at more than just a portrait of an individual.

dialogue.text: You are looking at the accumulated knowledge of a genius who blended art, science and magic to create a profound meditation on what it means to be human.
dialogue.zh: 你看到的是一位天才融合藝術、科學與魔法，對人類意義深刻冥想的累積知識。
dialogue.ja: あなたは芸術、科学、魔法を融合させ、人間とは何かを深く考察した天才の蓄積された知識を見ているのです。
dialogue.local: You are looking at the accumulated knowledge of a genius who blended art, science and magic to create a profound meditation on what it means to be human.
dialogue.en: You are looking at the accumulated knowledge of a genius who blended art, science and magic to create a profound meditation on what it means to be human.

dialogue.text: Whether she is Mona Lisa, Lagerkonda or Lagerkond, she is the face of a revolution in art.
dialogue.zh: 無論她是蒙娜麗莎、拉格孔達或拉格孔德，她都是藝術革命的象徵。
dialogue.ja: 彼女がモナリザであれ、ラ・ジョコンダであれ、芸術革命の顔です。
dialogue.local: Whether she is Mona Lisa, Lagerkonda or Lagerkond, she is the face of a revolution in art.
dialogue.en: Whether she is Mona Lisa, Lagerkonda or Lagerkond, she is the face of a revolution in art.
